title: Stapel realtime wire envelope v1
description: Every frame on a stapel-realtime socket, in both directions. The envelope is shared with stapel_core.comm.signal(), which builds exactly this shape and hands it to the transport; the transport forwards it to the socket verbatim. An L1 library normally publishes no schemas; this one is the deliberate exception (spec 4.1) because the envelope is a contract between a backend consumer and a browser client written by different hands, and it joins the events.json family when that lands.

v.description: Envelope version. A client that does not know this number must fail loudly rather than guess the shape underneath.

type.description: Either one of the ten protocol frame types listed in $defs.protocol_frame_types, or a SIGNAL's own type (e.g. 'recording.status'). The two share one field, which is why stapel_core.comm.signal() refuses to let a signal claim a protocol name: a consumer would read a courtesy frame as protocol. A frame whose type is not in the reserved list is a signal.

payload.description: Frame body. Its shape belongs to the module, except for the substrate's own frames described below.

seq.description: Monotonic per-stream sequence of a PERSISTED row. Frame kind is structural, not a flag: a journal frame (replay/live) carries seq, and an ephemeral one cannot, because nothing persisted it. A client tells the two apart by asking whether this key is present.

stream.description: Canonical stream key <mod>:<scope_type>:<scope_id>[:<topic>], built by stapel_core.comm.stream_key(). Redundant under the v1 socket-per-stream topology and populated anyway, so a future multiplexed socket can route on it without a v2 envelope.

protocol_frame_types.description: The ten names the protocol owns fleet-wide; stapel_core.comm.signals.RESERVED_FRAME_TYPES is the authority and the substrate's tests check the two against each other. 'replay_done' is the one frame the substrate emits that the core's reserved set does not yet cover (reported upstream).

hello.description: Client -> server. Subscribe and resume: 'I have everything up to last_seq'. Omitted or 0 means 'I have nothing'. Re-authorized on every hello, not only on connect.

welcome.description: Subscription accepted. server_seq is the highest sequence the module has persisted for this stream (absent on an ephemeral stream, which has no journal).

replay_done.description: Catch-up finished; everything after this frame is live.

resync.description: The resume gap was wider than the replay window, so nothing is replayed: re-hydrate over the module's HTTP pagination and reconnect with the fresh last_seq. Not an error — the socket stays open, and there is no infinite rewind by design.

kick.description: Rights were withdrawn while the socket was open. Sent immediately before close 4410; reconnecting will not help until access changes.

error.description: A refusal that does not close the socket (except on repeated bad envelopes, which closes 4400, and on a failed re-authorization, which closes 4403).
